t: Maximum Number of Non-overlapping Palindrome Substrings
o: Pick as many disjoint palindromic substrings of length ≥ k as possible. Greedy insight: finishing each chosen palindrome as early as possible leaves maximal room, and it suffices to check palindromes of length exactly k or k+1 starting at each position — any longer palindrome contains a palindromic core arrangement such that if no length-k or k+1 palindrome starts at i, none of any length does (its length-k prefix would fail symmetrically). Example 1: at i=0, "aba" (len 3) is a palindrome → take it, jump to i=3; at i=4, "dbbd" (len 4 = k+1) → take it; total 2. Example 2: no even-length palindrome ≥ 2 exists → 0. With n ≤ 2000, even O(n²) palindrome checks fit.
k: Greedy: take the earliest-ending valid palindrome, then continue after it.
It suffices to test lengths k and k+1 at each start position.
Expand-around-center gives palindrome radii in O(n²) total, well within limits.

a.i: Precompute isPal[i][j] with interval DP, then greedily scan: at position i, take the shortest palindromic substring starting at i with length ≥ k, jump past it; else advance one.
s: Scan i from 0; find minimal j ≥ i+k−1 with isPal[i][j].
If found, count++ and i = j+1; else i++.
a.t: O(n²) — DP fill dominates; scan adds O(n²) worst case

a.n: Approach 2: Length k / k+1 Greedy with Expand-Around-Center (Optimal)
a.i: Only lengths k and k+1 need testing at each start: a palindrome of length L ≥ k starting at i implies either its length-k prefix or a suitable k+1 window is itself a palindrome, so missing both means no valid palindrome starts at i. Expand-around-center verifies each check in O(n).
s: Define pal(i, j) returning the full palindrome length centered at (i, j) via expansion.
Scan i; if pal(i, i+k−1) ≥ k, count and i += k.
Else if pal(i, i+k) ≥ k+1, count and i += k+1; else i += 1.
a.t: O(n²) worst case (expansion per position), typically much faster

w: The k/k+1 greedy is elegant but its correctness proof is subtle — in an interview, present the DP-table greedy first (obviously correct) and offer the optimized version as an improvement. Pitfall: k = 1 makes every character a palindrome, answer = n. Also ensure jumps use the matched length, not k. Follow-up: maximize total length instead of count, or allow overlapping selections.
